title: WPSB/347/2012 of DR GYANENDRA PRASAD and OTHERS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 347 of 2012
Dr. Gyanendra Prasad and others .............. Petitioners

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .............. Respondents
Present: Mr. Arvind Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the petitioners.
 Mr. K.P. Upadhyay, Chief Standing Counsel with Mr. N.S.
 Pundir, brief holder for the State/respondent Nos.1 and 2.
 Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for respondent No.3.

Coram : Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
JUDGMENT
BARIN GHOSH, C.J. (Oral)
(Miscellaneous Application with R.A. No. 4593 of 2012
 Rejoinder affidavit is accepted on record. Application
made therefor is disposed of.
(Writ Petition (S/B) No. 347 of 2012)
Petitioners were appointed as Chikitsaks on contract.
Many other Chikitsaks were appointed on contract. The
Government decided that the available posts of Chikitsaks under
the Uttarakhand Ayush (Ayurvedic and Unani) Department Group
'B' Service Rules, 2010 be filled up. A requisition to that effect
was given. Subsequent thereto, Rule 8 of the said Rules was
amended and thereby a significant age relaxation was given to
contractual Chikitsaks, but for the selection year 2010-2011. All
the petitioners were appointed on contract in the month of June
2010. Petitioners, accordingly, responded to the corrigendum that
was published by the Commission. In the corrigendum, it was
indicated that whichever Chikitsak was within the advertised age
after adding 10 years of age in between 1st July, 2010 and 30th
June, 2011 will be eligible to respond to the advertisement. There

2
is no dispute that the petitioners were within the advertised age
after adding 10 years of age in between 1st July, 2010 and 30th
June, 2011. Despite that, the Commission has not accorded the age
relaxation to the petitioners and hence, the present writ petition.
2. It is the contention of the Commission that in order to
have age relaxation, it was obligatory on the part of the petitioners
to work continuously for one or more than one year. It is the
contention of the Commission that the selection year being 2010-
2011, it was obligatory on the part of the petitioners to work atleast
for one year on or before 1st July, 2010. It is the contention of the
Commission that only when the petitioners had worked as such,
they, in terms of the amended provision of Rule 8 of the said
Rules, would acquire eligibility for maximum 10 years' relaxation
in the upper age limit. The learned counsel for the petitioners
submitted that as on the date of publication of the corrigendum,
petitioners have already served for more than one year, inasmuch
as, they were appointed on contractual basis, sometimes in the
month of June 2010, whereas the corrigendum was issued on 13th
April, 2012.
3. The fact remains that the amended Rules granted
relaxation for the selection year 2010-2011, provided the persons
seeking relaxation have already worked for one or more than one
year as contractual Chikitsaks. Rule 3 (l) of the said Rules provides
that a period of twelve months commencing from first day of July
of a calendar year shall be regarded as the year of recruitment.
Rule 14 of the said Rules provides that the appointing authority
shall determine and intimate to the Commission the number of
vacancies to be filled during the course of the year. Therefore,
during the selection year 2010-2011 recourse will be taken to
supplying vacancies arising during the course of year, i.e. during
the period 1st July, 2009 - 30th June, 2010. The vacancies that have
arisen during the year of recruitment 1st July, 2009 - 30th June,

3
2010 would be supplied during the selection year 2010-2011.
During the selection year 2010-2011, if a Chikitsak has served the
Government for one year or more than one year, he will be entitled
to the age relaxation. Since the selection year is 2010-2011, the
Chikitsaks seeking the relaxation must have had joined atleast one
year before 30th June, 2011 as the selection year 2010-11 will come
to an end on 30th June, 2011.
4. The Commission was of the view that in order to take
advantage of the relaxation during the selection year 2010-2011, a
contractual Chikitsak must have had served atleast for one year by
the end of the year of recruitment or during the course thereof and
as the petitioners were appointed only in June 2010 and they
having not served atleast for one year before 1st July, 2010, they
would not be entitled to the relaxation.

5. As aforesaid, year of recruitment is a period of twelve
months commencing from 1st day of July of a calendar year.
According to Rule 14, appointing authority is obliged to determine
and intimate to the Commission the number of vacancies to be
filled during the course of the year. Therefore, the appointing
authority will determine vacancies for the year commencing from
1st July of a calendar year. The vacancies, which have arisen
during the course of the year, can only be determined at the end of
the year. Therefore, the vacancies were determined for the period
1st July, 2009 - 30th June, 2010. Those were to be filled up during
the year 2010-2011. During that year, if a contractual Chikitsak
has served atleast for one year, he would be entitled to the benefit
of age relaxation. The fact remains that the selection year 2010-
2011 will come to an end on 30th June, 2011. The fact also remains
that at the end of the selection year, i.e. as on 30th June, 2011,
petitioners have already served for one year, without any dispute,
as Contractual Chikitsaks.

4
6. In the circumstances, rejection of the claim of the
petitioners for being considered for appointment was inappropriate.
Petitioners, having worked for one year as on 30th June, 2011, had
acquired eligibility for obtaining relaxation for the selection year
2010-2011.
7. We, accordingly, allow the writ petition and direct
that the petitioners be considered as candidates for the
appointments in question and they be also put into the selection
process.
(U.C. Dhyani, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C.J.)
 15.10.2012 15.10.2012
P. Singh
